title: The Clockwork Crate
verdict: Soren Ward was responsible for the disappearance of a prototype navigation chip.
intent: Soren Ward wanted to hide a failed private project by stealing a working chip.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the calibration lead had permission to run the reboot after others left.
Remove a prototype navigation chip from its checked location.
Hide the item in a battery calibration drawer with a removable foam tray.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a prototype navigation chip disappeared from a campus robotics laboratory after a navigation demo.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the access panel opened during a scheduled firmware reboot.
The physical trace was two missing screws arranged beside the wrong tray.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a torque screwdriver with a chipped blue handle.
The item could be concealed in a battery calibration drawer with a removable foam tray.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the calibration lead knew the reboot cycle temporarily disabled the door camera.
The access pattern mattered because the calibration lead had permission to run the reboot after others left.
The motive was to hide a failed private project by stealing a working chip.

a visitor asking too many questions about the chip
